script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: title page, Pip the robot owl under a night sky

script_8to10.text: Pip is a small robot owl. She reads the news each night. Tonight, one story makes her feathers fluff up.
script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: Pip reading, feathers fluffed in surprise

script_8to10.text: Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft started a program called PRAISE. It helps new software engineers use AI tools well. Software engineers write the code that makes apps work.
script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: a university and a tech office linked by a banner reading PRAISE

script_8to10.text: The new engineers take classes online. They also get a coach who knows the job well.
script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: a young engineer at a laptop with an older coach beside them

script_8to10.text: Jace Watson's college did not teach him much about AI tools. A leader saw that AI helps skilled engineers more than new ones. Maybe new tools feel hard when no one shows you how.
script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: a lone figure facing a steep stack of unfamiliar tools

script_8to10.text: Mark Russinovich is a leader at Microsoft. He said AI does not remove the need for new engineers. Pip likes that. Everyone has to start somewhere.
script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: a leader speaking on a small stage, Pip nodding from a perch

script_8to10.text: Now the engineers learn in class and with a coach. Their classes can count toward a master's degree.
script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: a bright classroom, graduation cap on a desk

script_8to10.text: Pip thinks smart tools work best with people who keep learning. Maybe one day you will learn with an AI tool and a good teacher.
script_8to10.scene_description: PLACEHOLDER: Pip settling down to sleep, soft stars

script_8to10.text: Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft launched PRAISE. New engineers get coaching from senior engineers at Microsoft. The idea started with a visit to CMU in October 2025.
